result.title: Visual-State Graph Memory for Streaming Video Understanding
result.summary: In streaming video understanding, the evidence needed to answer a question may have already left the recent-frame window. Keeping all frames does not scale with video length, while dropping older frames limits the model's ability to reason about the past. We propose Visual-State Graph (VSG), a training-free memory that stores the state of a stream rather than the raw sequence of frames. VSG represents the stream as a graph of objects and their relations, together with a log of events; similar to a dynamically evolving scene graph. An object observed repeatedly is represented by one persistent node, with a timestamped history of how its state changes. To determine whether a newly mentioned object already exists in the graph, we compare the relations it takes part in with those of stored objects. We build this memory as the video arrives, before the questions are known. When a question arrives, we retrieve relevant objects and events alongside recent frames under a fixed input budget. Our evaluation spans four streaming-video benchmarks and seven open-source vision-language models ranging from 7B to 32B parameters. Under matched input budgets, VSG improves reasoning about the past while preserving real-time understanding.

AI.brief_summary: 提出无需训练的 Visual-State Graph 流式视频记忆：将视频流抽象为对象及关系的动态场景图和带时间戳的事件日志，用关系匹配合并重复对象，并在问题到来时于固定输入预算下检索相关对象、事件与近期帧。
AI.relevance_reason: 其以实体关系和状态历史替代原始帧堆叠，直接涉及视觉证据保存与筛选、有限预算下的过去信息使用，可为 LVR 的持久视觉状态表示和证据选择提供对照，但需核查图记忆是否真正被 VLM 推理使用及关系匹配的可靠性。
